# find a useful way to cleanup pip, gem, composer, npm

Find a repeatable way to prune globally installed language packages. The aliases `pip+`, `gem+`, `npm+`, `composer+` upgrade everything that is installed ([bin/lib/aliases.bash](../../bin/lib/aliases.bash)), but nothing ever removes the packages that were installed once for an experiment. The sketch is a declarative list and a tool that reconciles the installation with it:

```bash
$ pip list | cleaner pack > packages.yml
$ cleaner clean pip
```

i.e. snapshot what is wanted, then delete everything not in the snapshot — the Brewfile model ([[DOT-64]]) applied to pip, gem, Composer and npm.
